title: Faculty Survey Questionnaire
purpose: This survey collects feedback for the Self-Assessment Report of the Mass Communication and Journalism Discipline. Your responses help improve teaching, facilities, and graduate outcomes.
confidentiality: This survey is strictly anonymous. Data will be aggregated for quality assurance purposes only. No individual will be identified in the reporting.
scale: 1 = Strongly Disagree / Very Poor | 2 = Disagree / Poor | 3 = Neutral / Average | 4 = Agree / Good | 5 = Strongly Agree / Excellent

questions.text: My teaching load allows adequate time for research, mentoring, and administrative duties.
Class sizes are appropriate for effective teaching and feedback.
I am involved in strategic planning and aware of the program's vision and mission.
The teacher-student ratio is reasonable.
I have sufficient academic autonomy to design courses and teaching methods.
The curriculum is reviewed regularly with input from media professionals and alumni.
Course Learning Outcomes are clearly aligned with Program Learning Outcomes.
I use interactive methods (studio work, case studies, fieldwork) alongside lectures.
Assessment focuses on analysis, production, and professional communication skills.
I maintain course files (plans, assessments, rubrics) for every course.
I provide timely feedback on student work.
The institution provides adequate support for research and creative work.
I am encouraged to publish and present in my field.
The university supports participation in training, seminars, or conferences.
There is a clear policy for incentives for research and teaching excellence.
Study leave policy supports faculty pursuing advanced degrees.
Studios, labs, and production spaces are adequate and available for teaching.
The library has sufficient books, journals, and media databases for teaching and research.
IT facilities (internet, computers, software) are adequate.
I have a dedicated workstation and a congenial office environment.
Faculty recruitment and promotion are transparent, fair, and merit-based.
There is a well-defined code of conduct for faculty and staff.
I am actively involved in academic guidance and counseling.
Performance evaluation (KPIs) is clear, fair, and communicated effectively.
What are the major challenges you face in teaching this program?
How can research and creative-work support be improved?
Are studios, labs, and the library adequate? What is missing?
What professional development should the university organize?
